clue.text: Drink and eat in possibly after one

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come after the numeral, so it leads the answer

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of and, eat and in could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An instruction to have a drink and a meal indoors, perhaps after one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' and 'eat' both look like the definition; only the drink is, and 'and eat in' is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea grown in Assam or Darjeeling is a familiar beverage.

clue.text: Employing a woman over fifty is quite usual

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the name sits above the numeral

parts.note: Norma is a woman's name
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Taking on a female worker past fifty is nothing out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ordinary and expected is quite usual.

clue.text: Truly stylish action

parts.note: in means fashionable or stylish
a deed is an action

explanation.surface: A claim that some act is genuinely chic.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an adverb affirming that something really is so.

clue.text: Approached a queen, being in dire straits

indicators.note: being in says the article and the royal letter sit inside the word for hardship

parts.note: need means poverty or hardship
R stands for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A royal drew near while in deep trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being in' puts AR inside NEED; R for Regina is a crossword convention for queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To come closer to something is to approach it.

clue.text: A solitary child before getting ahead

indicators.note: getting ahead says the word for before goes in front of the child

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A lonely youngster who wants to get on in life.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit or recluse is a solitary, a person who lives alone.

clue.text: The fool takes a piece of cake to start nibbling

parts.note: something that is a piece of cake is simple, easy

indicators.note: start points to the opening letter of the word nibbling

explanation.surface: A silly person helps himself to a slice of gateau and begins to nibble.
explanation.definitionFit: A gullible, foolish person is a dolt or idiot.

clue.text: A lawyer railing about a highly-regarded person

indicators.note: about says the railing word goes around the saint

parts.note: a railing is a barrier
a saint, ST, is a person held in high regard

explanation.surface: An attorney complains loudly about some celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'railing' looks like ranting, but it is a fence; a saint is the highly-regarded person.
explanation.definitionFit: A British advocate who argues cases in the higher courts is a counsel.

clue.text: It's trendy to arrange for individual treatment

indicators.note: to arrange signals that the letters of it's and trendy are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A fashion tip about organising personal care.
explanation.definitionFit: The care of teeth is treatment given patient by patient in the chair.

clue.text: In time a painter will get much abuse

indicators.note: In says the painter goes inside the word for time

parts.note: tide is an old word for time or season
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: Eventually an artist will suffer a lot of insults.
explanation.walkthrough: Tide as a word for time survives in Yuletide; RA is a Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech is a harangue full of abuse.

clue.text: Acquired some personal letters

parts.note: reads like receiving post, but means earning letters such as BA to put after one's name

explanation.surface: Someone has received private correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing a degree earns initials like BA after the name.

clue.text: Dash for the hard stuff

explanation.surface: A splash of something strong.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigour and energy is dash, and distilled liquor like gin is the hard stuff.

clue.text: Dread injury to perverse stunt-man

indicators.note: injury to signals that the word dread is damaged into a new order

parts.note: perverse here means wicked

explanation.surface: A stuntman fears getting hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injury to' turns DREAD into DARED, followed by EVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless risk-taker who performs dangerous feats is a stunt-man.

clue.text: Separate the fibres of rags

definitions.meaning: to comb out wool or flax

explanation.surface: Pulling apart old cloth into threads.
explanation.definitionFit: Carding wool loosens fibres, and making fun of someone is ribbing them.

clue.text: Places intended for development

parts.note: reads like building plots, but means rooms where photographic film is developed

explanation.surface: Sites earmarked for building projects.
explanation.definitionFit: Film is processed in unlit rooms by photographers.

clue.text: A sot, since reformed, called for a halt

indicators.note: reformed signals that the letters of a sot since are shaped anew

explanation.surface: A drunkard who has mended his ways wanted to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopping or ending is a halt.

clue.text: Many a one denounced cut

parts.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals, a large number
an ace is a one on dice or cards
to rate is to scold or berate

explanation.surface: Lots of single people were condemned.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn or gashed flesh is cut.

clue.text: Quietly quarter a vegetable

parts.note: p is piano, quietly in music
E for east is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Softly divide a vegetable into four.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round green seed from a pod is a vegetable.

clue.text: Parking with little hesitation, get by

indicators.note: with places the two pieces side by side

parts.note: P is the sign for parking
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Finding a parking space with only a short pause, you manage.
explanation.definitionFit: Per is a preposition meaning by means of, as in per post.

clue.text: A mammal seen in the sea periodically

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'A mammal seen in the sea periodically (3)': no reading of 'seen in the sea periodically' gives PE or APE, likely an OCR misreading; no scan.
annotationWithheld.clue: A mammal seen in the sea periodically

clue.text: Mean to get a beverage and be off

indicators.note: off says the letters of be come away from a beverage

explanation.surface: Plan to grab a drink and then leave.
explanation.definitionFit: An arithmetic mean is the average of a set.

clue.text: An explorer-one given all-round support

indicators.note: given all-round says the support surrounds the word one

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar

explanation.surface: An adventurer who gets backing on every side.
explanation.definitionFit: The first to open up new territory is a trailblazer.

clue.text: Growing regret

definitions.meaning: a herb, something growing in the garden
regret means to be sorry for

explanation.surface: Sorrow that keeps getting bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter garden herb is a growing plant, and to repent is to regret.

clue.text: Virtuous prig housed in converted hut

indicators.note: housed in puts prig inside the rearranged hut
converted says the letters of hut are changed into another order

explanation.surface: A goody-goody lives in a renovated shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' reshuffles the shed's letters, and 'housed in' lodges the prig within them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone honest and principled is morally sound.

clue.text: Destiny is settled by the week-end

parts.note: the end of the word week is K
a bill met is a bill settled

explanation.surface: Fate is decided by Saturday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' places K beside IS and MET.
explanation.definitionFit: Fate or fortune is destiny.

clue.text: Continue to do the cleaning for the ferryman

parts.note: to char is to work as a cleaner
on means continue, as in carry on

explanation.surface: Keep cleaning for the man who runs the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the ferryman rows souls across the Styx.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the boatman carries the dead over the river Styx.

clue.text: Putting a gem in new setting can be a problem

indicators.note: new setting says the letters of a gem in are placed in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Mounting a jewel in a fresh setting can be tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle or mystery is a problem to solve.

clue.text: The guy swallowed a lot, though furious

parts.note: he refers to a man
ate means swallowed
D is 500 in Roman numerals, a lot

explanation.surface: The man ate a great deal while in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Angry and passionate is heated.

clue.text: Returning soldiers with little cash left port

indicators.note: Returning says the soldiers' letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, soldiers
change is coins, a little cash

explanation.surface: Soldiers coming back with some coins quit the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns RA into AR; Archangel is a port in northern Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Archangel on the White Sea is a Russian harbour city.

clue.text: Dreadful lout, a Western desperado

indicators.note: Dreadful signals that the letters of lout are mangled

explanation.surface: A horrible yob, a Wild West gunslinger.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit on the run from the law is a desperado.

clue.text: Building material as a whole

explanation.surface: Construction supplies considered in their entirety.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravel mixed into concrete is aggregate, and a sum total is the aggregate.

clue.text: Do more maybe when tied up

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of do more could be put differently

explanation.surface: Achieve more perhaps once you are bound.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat tied up at a quay is secured.

clue.text: Exemplary colours?

parts.note: exemplary suggests benchmarks; colours are regimental flags

explanation.surface: Flags held up as a model.
explanation.definitionFit: Benchmarks are norms, and regimental flags carried in battle are banners.
